title: Teaching himself clarinet and transposing parts
summary: Howard says fiddle and clarinet are alike, practices by fingering silently, and recalls transposing eight clarinet parts for his first theater job.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

No. They're my own way. Yeah. I got a sense that if no one or something isn't right, I can study and get it right. I can do that. I got two ways of practicing for somebody that's sleeping. I mean like theater pit. Yeah, in the old days. I remember the first job I got was with Earth Contagion, to do the clarionet. And they come to these eight clarionet parts. I go downtown the next day and buy me the eight clarionet and the thing sounds way off. You know, it's a tone and a half lower. Yes. And all that tone bothered my ear. And I look at him and I said, it sounds like the devil to me, you know. I took those parts home and transposed them. I'm looking at the transposer. All by yourself? Well, many times, you know, like a singer comes and makes a rehearsal. And we got the music down and she saw horses the next night and put it maybe a tone and a half, two tones down. Well that was easy with the fiddle. But not with that clarionet, you know. I didn't do it an hour because I've been on it too long, you know. But then, I don't know. But that's what I had to do and I took that clarionet back. All that thing.
